memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "Then his sister asked Pharaoh's daughter, "Shall I go and get one of the Hebrew women to nurse the baby for you?" "Yes, go," she answered. So the girl went and got the baby's mother." - Exodus 2:7-8 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Look at what God does in two verses. A slave mother had surrendered her son to the river. Now she is being invited into the palace to care for that very son — with royal permission.

No one planned this. Miriam simply spoke up at the right moment. Pharaoh's daughter simply said yes. And a family that had lost everything was handed back the thing they had grieved.

This is what Scripture calls providence: God quietly arranging ordinary conversations and small decisions to accomplish what no one could have engineered. There is no thunder here, no angel, no voice from heaven. Just a brave girl asking a question.

You may look back on your own life and see moments like this — a chance meeting, a delayed train, a job you did not get. At the time it felt random. Now you see a hand at work.

The God who arranged this is the same God working in the small details of your week today.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Where can I trace God's quiet providence in my past?
2. Is there a moment today where I should simply speak up?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Lord, thank You that You are working in details I never notice. Give me courage to speak and act when the moment comes. Amen.
